title: House Robber II
statement: Same as House Robber, but the houses stand in a circle, so the last house is a neighbour of the first. You cannot rob two neighbouring houses. Return the most cash you can take in one night.

example.caption: The two 2s touch across the circle, so only one can be robbed. Rob the 3 alone: 3.

idea.sentence: In a circle the first and last houses cannot both be robbed, so solve the straight row without the first house and the one without the last, and take the larger answer.

jargon.plain: What one table cell stands for. Here: the best loot from the first k houses of a straight row.
Turning a new problem (a circle) into copies of one you can already solve (a row).

watch.inputHint: One list of house values in a circle, e.g. [2,3,2]

rows.name: Try every subset
rows.note: Choose a set and check each neighbouring pair, including first with last.

rows.name: Two row DPs
rows.note: Two passes of about n cells each. A table per row.

rows.name: Two rows, two variables
rows.note: Each row only reads the two previous cells, so two numbers per row are enough.

fast.takeaway: The circle adds one rule. Cutting the circle open at that rule gives two ordinary rows.

stages.title: Cut the circle
stages.note: One house is a special case. Otherwise the first and last cannot both be used, so make two rows.

stages.title: Skip the last house
stages.note: Run the row DP on houses 0 to n - 2.

stages.title: Skip the first house
stages.note: Run the row DP on houses 1 to n - 1.

stages.title: Row base cells
stages.note: dp[0] = 0 and dp[1] is the first house of the row.

stages.title: Skip or rob
stages.note: dp[k] is the larger of dp[k - 1] (skip) and dp[k - 2] + loot (rob).

stages.title: Take the better row
stages.note: The answer is the larger of the two row results.

edges.title: One house
edges.why: With one house the first and the last are the same house, and cutting it out of both rows would leave nothing. Return it directly.

edges.title: Two houses
edges.why: They are neighbours. Each row has one house, so the answer is the larger one.

edges.title: Wrap trap
edges.why: The two 10s touch across the circle. The best is a 10 plus one of the 1s.

edges.title: Three equal
edges.why: Every house touches both others, so only one can be robbed.

gotchas.text: Do not run the plain row solution on the whole list and hope. It may pick both ends. Splitting into two rows rules that out.
n = 1 must be handled first. The two rows would both be empty, and returning 0 would be wrong.
nums.slice(1) and nums.slice(0, -1) copy the array. Passing lo and hi bounds into one helper avoids the copies.
nums[1:] and nums[:n-1] share memory with nums and cost nothing, but never append to them. Bounds, as here, avoid any aliasing worries.

recap.key: A circle means skip the first house or skip the last. Run the House Robber row DP on both and take the max.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(n), or O(1) with two variables per row.
moves: If there is one house, return it
Each row: dp[k] = max(dp[k - 1], dp[k - 2] + loot); answer is the max of the two rows
